newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam trial hears demand for death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam trial hears demand for death penalty.

text.p: Vietnam's biggest corruption trial entered its sixth day on Wednesday with the prosecution demanding the death penalty for four leading defendants.
State papers were plastered with details down to the facial expressions of those likely to be affected as the demand for the firing squad was read out in a packed Ho Chi Minh City court.

"Pham Huy Phuoc looked upwards, Tran Quang Vinh looked down, Le Minh Hai lost all humour from his face and Le Duc Canh tried to keep his composure but his expression wilted," the Lao Dong newspaper said.
In addition to the death penalty, the prosecution is calling for a range of jail terms for 16 other defendants.
Among these is life imprisonment for one person, but comparatively lenient terms of less than five years for two former top banking officials.
The trial centres around allegations of massive corruption at the Ho Chi Minh City trading firm Tamexco and has become a showcase for Hanoi's resolve to tackle endemic graft.
The firm is affiliated to the ruling Communist Party and several of those implicated have close links to some of the most powerful people in Vietnam.
Although foreign journalists have been refused permission to attend the trial, Vietnam's state-controlled media has been having a field day.
In addition to blow-by-blow accounts, Wednesday's media coverage included editorials condemning corruption and the related issue of abuse of land-rights.

"Together with material losses corruption is a national danger and internal enemy causing serious consequences and obstacles for the renovation (reform) process...providing fertile soil for peaceful evolution," said the official Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) daily, reflecting a broader media tone.
The trial is expected to run for several more days.
